_notes: The lamps are lit in the wrong order and the Lamplighters are nowhere. The rag-wraith is the lesson about declining a fight.
Scenes 12-17 of the prologue as it was before the split; `--scene story:<index>` still counts across the whole prologue, not within this file.

lines: Something is wrong tonight, and it is not the wisp. No pigeons. Pigeons are never quiet; quiet is against their religion.
The lamps on Needle Lane are lit wrong — and the Lamplighters never miss. The dog at Number Twelve is awake and does not bark, which it has never once failed to do.
Halfway down, the fog stops being fog.
It has sleeves. A collar. The shape of a person who is not in it — and every cut thread on this street is running towards it, like water finding a drain.
It turns what it has instead of a face towards me. Whatever unpicked the lamps is still working, and I am standing in its light.

notes: ❋ GUILE, the green patience — and MOONLIGHT, which is hers. Moonlight is WILD: one Moonlight card pays for anything you own.

coach.text: Nothing was healed on the walk here. Your heart, your spool and every action's remaining uses carried straight over from the wisp — one night, one budget, all the way to the end of it.
A RAG-WRAITH: clothes whose owner is missing. Not dead — missing. It is above your weight, and it knows it.
Guile in hand, which is what the LOAF wants. New energy, new action, first fight for both.
PURR heals 2 a turn for two turns — but it breaks the moment you are hit. Purr behind a guard, never in the open.

CONCENTRATE, for when the hand is empty and the spool is not: give up the whole turn to will one spent energy back onto the top of the deck. You draw it NEXT turn. The wraith still moves. Twice a fight, and no more.
And you do not have to win this. SLIP AWAY is a real answer — though it gets its telegraphed move in as you go.

lines: Three streets before I stop, and I stop because my legs decide it, not me.
Nothing followed. Nothing is missing. Ash: one. The weather: nothing. I would like that entered in the record.
And yet: it was not hunting me. It was WORKING. Whatever it is doing to this street, I interrupted about as much as a fly interrupts a window.
It comes apart in the middle of the road, and the threads it was pulling go slack.
That was not supposed to be possible, and I do not feel clever about it. I feel like something let go.
